content.value_statement: Database work slows down when table relationships and tenant rules are hard to find. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a focused Supabase schema reference for safer query planning.
actual_capabilities: Summarizes core Empathy Ledger Supabase tables by domain.
Shows foreign-key relationships across tenant, profile, story, media, and moderation tables.
Provides example SQL queries for common storytelling and theme analysis tasks.
Highlights tenant isolation requirements for Supabase queries.
Points users to detailed table and relationship reference files.
limitations: Does not connect to Supabase or run live database queries.
Does not verify whether the documented schema matches production.
Does not include migration files or RLS policy definitions.
Focuses on Empathy Ledger schema concepts, not general Supabase administration.

use_cases.title: Plan tenant-safe queries
use_cases.description: Use the relationship map to include tenant filters before writing Supabase queries.

use_cases.title: Find the right content tables
use_cases.description: Identify where stories, transcripts, media assets, themes, and quotes are stored.

use_cases.title: Understand data model dependencies
use_cases.description: Review how profiles, organisations, projects, and stories connect before changing features.

prompt_templates.title: Find a table
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the supabase skill to tell me which tables store stories, transcripts, and themes.

prompt_templates.title: Explain relationships
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the supabase skill to explain how profiles, storytellers, stories, and transcripts relate.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a safe query
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the supabase skill to draft a tenant-aware query for published stories with their themes.

prompt_templates.title: Review data access design
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the supabase skill to review this feature idea for missing tenant filters and table joins.

output_examples.input: Which tables connect a story to its author and media?
output_examples.output: A story links to profiles through storyteller_id and author_id, and to media_assets through featured_media_id.

output_examples.input: How should I query stories for one tenant?
output: Look up the user profile to get tenant_id.
Filter stories by tenant_id before applying status or theme filters.
Join related tables only after tenant scope is established.

output_examples.input: Where are AI analysis results documented?
output_examples.output: The skill lists transcript_analysis_results for versioned analysis, narrative_themes for extracted themes, and knowledge_chunks for RAG embeddings.

best_practices: Ask for tenant-aware query examples when working with shared data.
Use the relationship reference before adding joins across profiles, stories, and projects.
Confirm live schema details in Supabase before applying production changes.
anti_patterns: Do not treat the reference as proof that production schema is current.
Do not write cross-tenant queries without an explicit tenant filter.
Do not use example UUID values or sample SQL as production-ready access control.

faq.question: Does this skill connect to my Supabase project?
faq.answer: No. It provides static reference material and does not open network connections.

faq.question: Can it run SQL queries?
faq.answer: No. It can help draft and explain queries, but it does not execute them.

faq.question: What database area does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers Empathy Ledger tables for tenants, profiles, stories, transcripts, media, themes, and governance workflows.

faq.question: Can it help with Row Level Security?
faq.answer: It highlights tenant isolation patterns, but it does not include full RLS policy definitions.

faq.question: Is it useful outside Empathy Ledger?
faq.answer: It is mainly useful for this schema, but the relationship patterns can inform similar Supabase projects.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
